slides.0.title: Burgenland
slides.0.subtitle: Land of reds and sweet wines
slides.1.title: Burgenland's six DACs
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Pannonian continental climate with hot, dry summers; about 11,500 ha in Burgenland (2024 data)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The six DACs
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Neusiedlersee, Leithaberg, Mittelburgenland, Eisenberg, Rosalia and Ruster Ausbruch
slides.1.content: Learn the list first, then each DAC's varieties and years.
slides.2.title: The red DACs
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Mittelburgenland (2005)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Blaufränkisch only; Klassik 12.5–13% and Reserve at least 13% (large oak or barrels)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Eisenberg
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Also Blaufränkisch-based: Klassik 12.5–13% and Reserve at least 13%
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Rosalia (2017)
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Based on Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt, and includes rosé
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Leithaberg
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Red (2008 vintage) at least 85% Blaufränkisch; white (2009 vintage) from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner
slides.2.content: Leithaberg has both red and white rules, with whites up to 13.5% abv.
slides.3.title: Neusiedlersee and Ruster Ausbruch
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Neusiedlersee reds
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Klassik (2011) at least 85% Zweigelt; Reserve (2010) at least 60% Zweigelt
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Neusiedlersee sweet wines
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Sweet styles from 2020, with at least 45 g/L residual sugar
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Ruster Ausbruch (2020)
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Ausbruch sweet wine from white Qualitätswein varieties; sources differ on the minimum KMW, so no threshold is given here
slides.3.content: Noble rot around Rust and the Neusiedler See underpins Ausbruch (see the Level 1 climate lesson).
slides.4.title: Diploma depth: the east, north and west shores of the lake
slides.4.highlights.0.title: East shore, Seewinkel: botrytis sweet wines
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Seewinkel east of the lake (e.g. Illmitz, Apetlon) is flat and sandy, dotted with shallow saline ponds; autumn mist and humidity make botrytis almost annual, making it the heart of Beerenauslese and TBA
slides.4.highlights.1.title: North shore: red wine
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Around Gols on the north shore it is warm and moderated by the lake, known for Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch and red blends, and is the backbone of Neusiedlersee DAC reds (common description)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: West shore, Rust: the history of Ausbruch
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Rust lies on the west shore, near the slopes of the Leithagebirge. In the 17th century Rust bought its status as a free town with money and wine, and Ausbruch sweet wine was the source of its wealth; today Ruster Ausbruch must meet TBA conditions (see Level 3)
slides.4.highlights.3.title: The south: Eisenberg schist
slides.4.highlights.3.content: Eisenberg in southern Burgenland is known for iron-rich schist, giving taut, mineral, spicy Blaufränkisch, in contrast to the fuller style from the heavier clays of Mittelburgenland (general description)
slides.4.content: One lake, three shores, three wines: sweet in the east, red in the north, Ausbruch and Leithaberg in the west.
